title: The team that is going to ring the Nasdaq bell
body:
## The Architect and His Timeline

The appointments did not arrive by coincidence. In August 2023, Bami Bastani joined Sivers Semiconductors as a Strategic Advisor — a title that, in semiconductor circles, rarely means what it says. By February 2024 he was Executive Chairman of the US subsidiary and Chairman of the Swedish parent. Six months later, a new CEO arrived. Eighteen months after that, the company filed PCAOB-aligned restated financials — the accounting standard required for a US public listing — and simultaneously nominated two new directors whose CVs read like a cross-border transaction checklist. The sequence is not coincidental. It is a programme.

Bastani is the architect. Forty-two years in the semiconductor industry have taken him from component roles at Intel and National Semiconductor through systems-on-chip at Fujitsu Micro to three separate tenures as a turnaround CEO at public companies: ANADIGICS, a III-V compound semiconductor maker that Wall Street had given up on; Trident Microsystems, a digital media chipmaker navigating a brutal cost cycle; and Meru Networks, an enterprise WiFi platform. Each was a listed company. Each required restructuring under quarterly earnings scrutiny. His final corporate role before arriving at Sivers was Senior Vice President at GlobalFoundries, the world's third-largest foundry, where he also served on the board of the Global Semiconductor Alliance. He is, in short, not a board ornament. He is the most experienced operating executive in the room, placed at the chairman seat specifically to translate a Swedish mid-cap photonics company into something a Nasdaq investor relations roadshow can sell.

## The CEO Who Invested in His Own Bet

Vickram Vathulya was appointed President and CEO on 19 August 2024, replacing Anders Storm. His credentials are unusual for a Stockholm-listed company: a PhD in Electrical Engineering from Lehigh University in Pennsylvania, an MBA from Berkeley Haas, and twenty-five years in semiconductors spanning geographies that track the industry's centre of gravity rather than Stockholm's. At NXP Semiconductors he ran RF and wireless business lines; at Maxim Integrated he grew the RF and wireless portfolio; at Maxim Semiconductors he revitalised what the company described as its "largest and most profitable" standard products division. His most recent pre-Sivers role was President of Nuvotronics, a compound-semiconductor and advanced-interconnect company, where he led what the company called a strategic, operational and cultural transformation.

> "We see a highly complementary fit between our high-performance DFB lasers and POET's innovative optical interposer platform," [Vathulya told the market](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market) at the announcement of the POET Technologies partnership in September 2025.

What distinguishes the appointment beyond the CV is the share commitment. At the time of his appointment, Vathulya agreed to subscribe to up to two million Sivers shares, subject to shareholder approval — a personal commitment valued at up to $1 million at prevailing prices. For a CEO inheriting an operating loss of SEK 177.8 million against revenue of SEK 306.6 million in fiscal 2025, that is not a symbolic gesture. A Lehigh PhD and Berkeley MBA running a Swedish-listed compound semiconductor company is not, as one analyst framing puts it, staffed for European institutional comfort. It is staffed for a Nasdaq investor day.

## The Door Was Already Open

The board member whose significance is most easily underweighted is Todd Thomson — and that would be a mistake. Thomson joined the Sivers board in 2021, three years before Bastani arrived and four years before the PCAOB restatement that crystallised the US-listing trajectory. That sequence matters: Thomson did not follow Bastani onto the board. If anything, he preceded him.

His CV is the most concentrated source of US capital-markets credibility on the board. He holds an MBA from Wharton and a BA in Economics from Davidson College. At Citigroup he served as CFO for five years, then as CEO of Citigroup Global Wealth Management — a $10 billion division — for two and a half years, and subsequently as CEO of Citigroup Alternative Investments. He chaired the Citi Pension Investment Committee. Before Citi, his career ran through Bain & Company, Booz Allen Hamilton, Barents Group and GE Capital, with advisory work at GlobalFoundries providing the semiconductor-specific thread. He currently serves as COO and CFO of Kairos Ventures, a US venture capital firm, and sits on the board of Actuate Therapeutics, as well as investment committees at Davidson College, the World Resources Institute and Dynasty.

A former Citi CFO who has served on investment committees at three institutions and currently runs the finances of a US VC firm does not join the board of a Stockholm small-cap to provide passive oversight. The Bastani-Vathulya-Thomson combination is unusually heavy on US public-company experience for a company at this market capitalisation — approximately SEK 22.7 billion, or roughly $2.2 billion at current exchange rates — and the concentration is deliberate. Thomson, in all probability, was the figure who opened the door.

## The Technical Floor

Karin Raj is not a finance professional, which is precisely the point. As CTO Europe at Nokia — an organisation that has navigated every major inflection point in wireless infrastructure from 2G through 5G — she carries direct operational authority in the exact intersection of domains Sivers sells into: telecommunications, satellite communications, semiconductors, photonics, sensors and nanotechnology. Her career has taken her through Ericsson and across geographies including the United States, China, India, France, Turkey and the Nordic countries. She led technical functions through multiple wireless-generation transitions and has domain exposure in AI, IoT and high-precision micro-mechanics.

At Sivers she chairs the Investment Committee — the board subcommittee with authority over capital expenditure decisions. That is the structural CTO function of the board: independent technical review of whether the product roadmap and capex allocation are coherent with what the market will actually require. For a company whose central thesis rests on the claim that InP DFB lasers are the irreplaceable upstream component in the co-packaged optics supply chain, having a sitting Nokia CTO Europe making the capex calls is not decoration. It is the credibility mechanism that keeps the roadmap honest.

## The Departures Are Not Symmetrical

Fällström leaves the board alongside two other directors: Tomas Duffy and Keith Halsey. But the three departures are not equivalent, and treating them as a bloc obscures what each represents.

Tomas Duffy is the institutional memory. He joined the Sivers board in 2016, became Chairman in 2018, and was present at every major structural decision in the company's modern history: the 2017 acquisition of CST Global (which became Sivers Photonics, the UK-based laser operation); the 2022 acquisition of MixComm; and the rebranding from Sivers IMA to Sivers Semiconductors. His pre-Sivers career at EKN Exportkreditnämnden — the Swedish state export credit agency, where he served as Director of Large Corporates and Head of Telecom from December 2010 to April 2017 — anchored the company's European institutional credibility through the growth-stage years when Swedish government-adjacent credibility mattered for access to capital and contracts. He holds a BSc from KTH, the Royal Institute of Technology, and retains concurrent board seats at CST Global Ltd., Stella Tech AB and Stella Tech Distribution AB. His departure is not a finding of fault. The transition to a US-listing-architect chairman made him surplus to the next phase rather than wrong for the previous one.

Erik Fällström's departure is different in character. He is a co-founder, currently CEO of DDM Debt, and controls approximately 11.8 per cent of Sivers' voting rights through DDM and the Fällström Family Office — a stake he retains after leaving the board. DDM has publicly stated that it wishes to drive Sivers "toward a broader investment company," a strategic vision in direct tension with the focused-operating-company narrative that a Nasdaq listing requires. Activist holding-company framing and a Nasdaq IPO pitch are incompatible. His departure from the board clears the room for a story Sivers can actually tell on a US roadshow; his continuing economic stake means the strategic tension does not disappear, it relocates to the shareholder register.

Keith Halsey was elected to the board at the 15 May 2024 AGM and is departing approximately thirteen months later. Public biographical detail on Halsey remains thin in the sources reviewed at the snapshot date — this is a genuine sourcing gap, not a basis for inference. The short tenure is consistent with a transitional appointment bridging the pre-Bastani board configuration and the US-listing-prep composition, but the AGM materials do not offer an explanation for his rotation, and speculation would outrun the available evidence.

## The Incoming Slate

Joakim Nideborn, nominated as Vice Chairman, is not a "broad CFO background" abstraction — he is the sitting CFO and Deputy CEO of HMS Networks AB, a Nasdaq Stockholm-listed industrial communications company where he has served since December 2017, with promotion to Deputy CEO in December 2021. His prior career ran through Axiell Group, Ixyz Consulting and Beijer Electronics. His stated focus at Sivers is primary oversight of the board for Nordic-region customers, employees and investors — the governance counterpart to Bastani's US-capital-markets orientation.

Helena Svancar is the most cross-border M&A-pedigreed director on the incoming board. She spent ten years at Deutsche Bank, rising to Managing Director and Head of Corporate Finance Nordics, then nearly five years as Head of M&A at Ericsson before joining Verdane, the Nordic growth-equity firm, as a Partner in September 2022. She holds a CEMS MSc in Finance and International Management from Stockholm School of Economics and the University of St. Gallen, and currently serves as a non-executive director at Onomondo and at Truecaller, where she chairs the Remuneration Committee. A former Deutsche Bank Head of Corporate Finance Nordics and former Ericsson M&A chief is the addition a board makes when it expects to execute cross-border transactions. Her appointment is signal-dense.

## Overhang

Two concurrent governance concerns shadow the AGM. Sweden's Economic Crime Authority (Ekobrottsmyndigheten) is examining possible market abuse violations connected to the Nasdaq dual-listing announcement, which leaked approximately forty-eight hours early via an anonymous account on X. The investigation is open as of the snapshot date; its outcome could materially affect investor sentiment in the weeks surrounding the listing mechanics. Separately, Sivers joins the MSCI Sweden Small Cap Index on 29 May 2026 — the same date Q1 results land under the new PCAOB reporting regime. Passive fund buying is mechanically forced to coincide with the first earnings release in the new accounting framework. That is an unusual collision of technical and fundamental catalysts, and it is not clear which will dominate.

## The Shape of the Board

Post-AGM, the Sivers board numbers five: Bastani as Executive Chairman, Vathulya running the operation from the CEO seat, Nideborn as Vice Chairman with Nordic-governance oversight, Thomson as the most credentialed US capital-markets figure on the board, and Raj as the technical anchor and Investment Committee chair. Svancar adds the M&A and cross-border transaction capability.

The Swedish founder-investor presence — Fällström's strategic vision for a holding company, Duffy's European institutional credibility function — is being cleared out. The shape that remains says Nasdaq New York. Four of the five directors carry primary professional identities in corporate-finance and transactional execution. For a company at approximately $2.2 billion market capitalisation, that concentration of financial-markets pedigree is not an accident of hiring. The only question the board composition leaves open is timing.
